title: DSES v0.2.0-rc8 Definition Artifacts
description: Six immutable, content-addressed definition artifacts. content_hash preimage: RFC 8785 canonical form with content_hash removed. Anchor evidence is PROHIBITED inside an artifact (it lives in artifact_anchored events), so timing evidence can improve without changing artifact identity. Prespecification is declared against an external cutoff, never against DSES ingestion order.

executable_rule.description: A machine-executable rule: identifier, SHA-256 of the actual code artifact bytes, and shipped conformance fixtures. Names are not code; the verifier recomputes the digest from the module and executes the fixtures.

code_artifact.description: Explicit locator for the bytes the digest covers. Without it, a second implementation receives a digest with no normative answer to 'of which object?', and must reverse-engineer a path convention private to one implementation.

locator.description: Package-relative path, or a locator appropriate to the media type (OCI descriptor, wheel filename, WASM module path).

parameters.description: Declared parameters a verifier needs to check the rule WITHOUT reading the reference module. A constant that lives only in one implementation's source is the same defect as a digest without a locator: it answers what to check but not from where.

membership_multiplicity.description: v0.2 supports one membership token per eligible decision instance. Repeated encounters are distinct decision instances and MUST use distinct tokens.

unit_of_analysis.description: The level at which metrics derived from this cohort may be reported. Declared BEFORE enrollment and anchored like every other definition, because a cohort assembled to evaluate an AI system and later re-cut per clinician is a different study than the one that was prespecified.

evaluation_criterion.description: The general criterion abstraction. criterion_type selects a specialization; the clinical reference standard is one of them, not the only one.

binary_validity_projection.description: Required because RAIR, RSR, SRF, and EAR are only defined over a binary validity partition (Section 8.2).

answer_space_semantics.description: The measurement semantics of answer_space. Alignment relations declare which semantics they are valid for; a relation defined by exact agreement is meaningless over an ordered space and vice versa.

agreement_statistic.description: The executable definition of the charter's agreement statistic, including how non-assessable assessments compare.

revision_protocol.description: How a determination may be revised. Without this, a revision citing no assessments escapes every charter constraint, which is a laundering path beside the one Section 6.10 closes.

assessment_free_methods.description: Methods that may resolve without citing new independent assessments. An adjudication resolved this way MUST NOT record an inter-adjudicator agreement statistic, since there are no assessments to compute it over.

deciding_role.description: Charter role authorized to decide an assessment-free revision.

alignment_relation.description: Required when the metric's definition depends on an alignment relation (EAR). Section 4: alignment relations are executable, digested, and fixtured like any other recomputation-affecting rule.

secondary_use_governance.description: Required before any metric may be derived at individual-clinician level. DSES makes per-clinician derivation mechanically trivial; this artifact makes it procedurally deliberate, prespecified, and attributable.

purpose.description: What the individual-level derivation is for. Quality improvement, credentialing, and litigation support are different purposes with different governance; a single artifact may not silently serve all three.

min_cell_size.description: Minimum denominator below which an individual-level metric MUST NOT be reported. A rate over a handful of eligible cases carries an interval so wide it cannot support any determination, and reporting the point estimate alone invites one anyway.

case_mix_adjustment.description: Without case-mix disclosure a clinician who takes harder cases is penalised by construction.

subject_notification.description: Whether and how the clinician whose record is being derived is informed.

purpose_code.description: Structured secondary-use purpose. High-stakes purposes trigger additional safeguards; the free-text purpose remains explanatory only.

decision_consequence.description: The maximum consequence the governance artifact authorizes the analysis to inform. DSES records this authorization; it does not establish the legal authority to impose the consequence.

max_observation_window_days.description: Maximum longitudinal window for an individual-level metric. The value is governance-defined rather than supplied by DSES; each metric must state its actual bounded window.

high_stakes_safeguards.description: Declared procedural safeguards. For credentialing, employment, litigation support, or regulatory oversight all four are required true. Actual compliance remains external to DSES.

governance_timing.description: Whether this authorization preceded the observations it governs. Prespecified relative to an analysis cutoff MUST NOT be used to imply prospective authorization of professional surveillance.

privacy_basis.description: Declared, not validated: DSES requires the declaration and binds it; it does not determine whether the selected legal basis is valid.

responsibility_assignments.description: Prospective binding of decision instances to responsible professionals, independent of later linkage. Cohort denominator closure does not confer clinician denominator closure: subject attribution derived only from linked trajectories lets a subject's failed linkages vanish from their own record.
